submitted.rationale: Index 0 (Nb0.504V0.496) gave the highest photocurrent, 6.7 µA, of the 3 measured. That beats the V-rich end (index 7, 5.5 µA) and the Nb-rich end (index 9, 1.6 µA). The results are consistent with a peak near the 1:1 NbVO5/NbVO4 stoichiometry. MACE puts NbVO5 near the hull (0.027 eV/atom), and the predicted gaps are about 3.5 eV and 1.8 eV. The merit budget is used up.

rejected.reason: Measured 1.6 µA; the Nb-rich side performs poorly
GP suggestion, not measured because the budget was used; it sits between index 0 and the weak Nb-rich trend

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): NbVO5 near-stable (0.027 eV/atom), MEGNet HSE gap 3.48 eV marginal vs 3.22 eV photons; V-rich side should absorb more (V5+ lowers gap), so start at the most V-rich end, index 7.
Support (exploratory): Nb4VO12-type Nb-rich phase predicted HSE gap 2.84 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so the Nb-rich end may absorb; measure index 9 to bracket the composition line.

Support: 1:1 NbVO4 polymorph predicted HSE gap 1.8 eV (strong absorber at 3.22 eV); together with NbVO5 near-hull, stoichiometric Nb:V≈1:1 (index 0) may host a single-phase peak between the measured V-rich (5.5 µA) and Nb-rich (1.6 µA) ends.
